title.raw: 卷113 官氏志九 Volume 113 Treatise 9: Official Ranks

sentences.zh: 百姓不能以自治，故立君以司牧；

translations.literal: The common people cannot govern themselves, and therefore a ruler is established to oversee and shepherd them;
translations.idiomatic: Because the people cannot govern themselves, a ruler is installed to shepherd them;

sentences.zh: 元首不可以獨斷，乃命臣以佐之。

translations.literal: The sovereign cannot decide all matters alone, and therefore ministers are appointed to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign cannot rule alone, so ministers are appointed to assist him.

sentences.zh: 然則安海內，正國家，非一人之力也。

translations.literal: Thus to pacify the realm within the seas and set the state aright is not the work of a single man.
translations.idiomatic: Securing the realm and putting the state in order, then, is not the achievement of one man alone.

sentences.zh: 書契已外，其事蔑聞，至於羲、軒、昊、頊之間，龍、火、鳥、人之職，頗可知矣。

translations.literal: Beyond the age of written records nothing is heard of these matters; but from the time of Fu Xi, Xuanyuan, Shaohao, and Zhuanxu, the offices of Dragon, Fire, Bird, and Man are fairly well known.
translations.idiomatic: Before written records nothing is known of such matters; yet from the age of Fu Xi, the Yellow Emperor, Shaohao, and Zhuanxu, the posts of Dragon, Fire, Bird, and Man are at least partly understood.

sentences.zh: 唐虞六十，夏商倍之，周過三百，是為大備。

translations.literal: Under Tang and Yu there were sixty offices; Xia and Shang doubled that number; Zhou had more than three hundred—this was the fullest development.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang and Yu there were sixty offices; the Xia and Shang doubled that figure; the Zhou exceeded three hundred—this was the fullest institutional array.

sentences.zh: 而秦、漢、魏、晉代有加減，罷置盛衰，隨時適務。

translations.literal: Yet Qin, Han, Wei, and Jin each added to or reduced these offices in turn, abolishing or establishing posts as they flourished or declined, adapting to the needs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin, Han, Wei, and Jin, offices were added or cut in each generation, posts abolished or revived with changing fortunes, always adjusted to the tasks of the time.

sentences.zh: 且國異政，家殊俗，設官命職，何常之有。

translations.literal: Moreover, when states differ in policy and families differ in custom, how can the establishment of offices and appointment of duties ever remain fixed?
translations.idiomatic: When every state has its own policies and every house its own customs, how could the design of offices and ranks ever stay the same?

sentences.zh: 帝王為治，禮樂不相沿；

translations.literal: When emperors and kings govern, rites and music are not carried on unchanged from age to age;
translations.idiomatic: Emperors and kings govern in their own way; rites and music are not handed down unchanged;

sentences.zh: 海內作家，物色非一用。

translations.literal: when those who found houses within the realm take office, the roles sought are not employed in a single way.
translations.idiomatic: and when founders of new houses rise within the realm, the talents they seek serve many different ends.

sentences.zh: 其由來尚矣。

translations.literal: The origins of this reach far back.
translations.idiomatic: This has been so since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 魏氏世君玄朔，遠統□臣，掌事立司，各有號秩。

translations.literal: The Wei clan for generations ruled the dark north, commanding distant subjects from afar; they set up offices to manage affairs, each with its title and rank.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the Wei ruled the far north, holding sway over distant subjects; they established bureaus to manage affairs, each with its own title and rank.

sentences.zh: 及交好南夏，頗亦改創。

translations.literal: When they entered friendly relations with the southern Xia states, they also made considerable reforms.
translations.idiomatic: Once they cultivated ties with the southern Chinese states, they introduced many reforms as well.

sentences.zh: 昭成之即王位，已命燕鳳為右長史，許謙為郎中令矣。

translations.literal: When Zhaocheng [Emperor Zhaowen] ascended the throne, he had already appointed Yan Feng Right Chief Clerk and Xu Qian Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaowen took the throne, he had already named Yan Feng Right Chief Clerk and Xu Qian Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 餘官雜號，多同於晉朝。

translations.literal: The remaining miscellaneous official titles largely matched those of the Jin dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Most other miscellaneous titles followed Jin usage.

sentences.zh: 建國二年，初置左右近侍之職，無常員，或至百數，侍直禁中，傳宣詔命。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianguo [387], the posts of Left and Right Personal Attendants were first established, without fixed quotas, sometimes reaching a hundred men; they attended duty within the inner palace and transmitted imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianguo year 2 (387), the posts of Left and Right Personal Attendants were created for the first time, with no fixed quota—sometimes numbering as many as a hundred—serving inside the palace and relaying edicts.

sentences.zh: 皆取諸部大人及豪族良家子弟儀貌端嚴，機辯才幹者應選。

translations.literal: Candidates were drawn from chieftains of the various tribes and from sons of eminent clans and good families who were dignified in bearing and quick-witted and capable.
translations.idiomatic: They were chosen from tribal chieftains and from sons of powerful clans and reputable families who were dignified in appearance and gifted with wit and ability.

sentences.zh: 又置內侍長四人，主顧問，拾遺應對，若今之侍中、散騎常侍也。

translations.literal: Four Chief Inner Attendants were also appointed to give counsel, remedy omissions, and respond to queries, like today's Palace Attendants and Regular Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Four Chief Inner Attendants were also set up to advise the throne, supply what was missing, and answer queries—the counterparts of today's Palace Attendants and Regular Attendants of the Fast Steed.

sentences.zh: 其諸方雜人來附者，總謂之「烏丸」，各以多少稱酋、庶長，分為南北部，復置二部大人以統攝之。

translations.literal: Various mixed peoples from other regions who came to submit were collectively called "Wuhuan"; according to their numbers they were titled chiefs or common chiefs, divided into a Northern and a Southern Division, and two Division Chiefs were again appointed to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: Various peoples from other regions who submitted were collectively termed "Wuhuan"; by their numbers they were styled chiefs or sub-chiefs, organized into northern and southern divisions, with two Division Chiefs appointed to govern them.

sentences.zh: 時帝弟觚監北部，子寔君監南部，分民而治，若古之二伯焉。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor's younger brother Gu supervised the Northern Division and the emperor's son Shijun supervised the Southern Division, dividing the people between them for governance, like the two regional lords of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor's brother Gu oversaw the north and his son Shijun the south, dividing the people between them in governance like the two great regional lords of old.

sentences.zh: 太祖登國元年，因而不改，南北猶置大人，對治二部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dengguo [386] under Emperor Taizu, the system was left unchanged; Chiefs were still appointed for north and south, each governing one division.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizu's first Dengguo year (386) the arrangement was kept; Chiefs were still set over north and south, each administering one division.

sentences.zh: 是年置都統長，又置幢將及外朝大人官。

translations.literal: That year a Chief Commander-in-Chief was appointed, and also Banner Generals and Outer Court Chief posts.
translations.idiomatic: That year a Chief Commander-in-Chief was created, along with Banner Generals and Outer Court Chiefs.

sentences.zh: 其都統長，領殿內之兵，直王宮；

translations.literal: The Chief Commander-in-Chief commanded the troops within the palace and was on duty at the royal residence;
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Commander-in-Chief led the palace guard and was stationed at the royal residence;

sentences.zh: 幢將員六人，主三郎衞士直宿禁中者。

translations.literal: there were six Banner Generals in post, in charge of the Third-Rank Guardsmen who stood night watch within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: six Banner Generals oversaw the Third-Rank Guardsmen on night duty in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 自侍中已下，中散已上，皆統之外朝大人，無常員。

translations.literal: From Palace Attendant downward and from Regular Palace Attendant upward—all were grouped under Outer Court Chiefs, without fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: From Palace Attendant down through Regular Palace Attendant up, all fell under Outer Court Chiefs, with no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 主受詔命，外使，出入禁中，國有大喪大禮皆與參知，隨所典焉。

translations.literal: They received edicts, served on missions abroad, and entered and left the inner palace; on great state mourning and great state ceremonies they all took part according to the duties they oversaw.
translations.idiomatic: They received edicts, went on missions abroad, and moved in and out of the palace; on major mourning and state rites they all took part according to their assigned duties.

sentences.zh: 天興元年十一月，詔吏部郎鄧淵典官制，立爵品。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Tianxing [398], an edict ordered Deng Yuan of the Ministry of Personnel to take charge of the official system and establish ranks of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Tianxing year 1 (398), an edict directed Deng Yuan, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, to oversee the official system and establish noble ranks.

sentences.zh: 十二月，置八部大夫、散騎常侍、待詔等官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the posts of Eight-Division Grandee, Regular Attendant of the Fast Steed, and Awaiting Edict were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the posts of Eight-Division Grandee, Regular Attendant of the Fast Steed, and Awaiting Edict were created.

sentences.zh: [1]其八部大夫於皇城四方四維面置一人，以擬八座，謂之八國常侍。

translations.literal: [1] One Eight-Division Grandee was placed on each of the four sides and four corners of the imperial city, to correspond to the Eight Excellencies; they were called Regular Attendants of the Eight States.
translations.idiomatic: [1] One Eight-Division Grandee was stationed on each side and corner of the imperial city, matching the Eight Excellencies; they were called Regular Attendants of the Eight States.

sentences.zh: 待詔侍直左右，出入王命。

translations.literal: Awaiting Edicts attended on duty at the ruler's side and carried royal commands in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting Edicts stood duty at the ruler's side and conveyed his commands.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，分尚書三十六曹及諸外署，凡置三百六十曹，令大夫主之。

translations.literal: In the third month of year 2, the thirty-six bureaus of the Secretariat and various outer offices were divided; three hundred sixty bureaus were established in all, each headed by a grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 2 the thirty-six Secretariat bureaus and various outer offices were split into three hundred sixty bureaus in all, each led by a grandee.

sentences.zh: 大夫各有屬官，其有文簿，當曹敷奏，欲以省彈駁之煩。

translations.literal: Each grandee had subordinate officials; when documents were involved, the responsible bureau would present them directly, intending to spare the trouble of review and rejection.
translations.idiomatic: Each grandee had subordinates; when paperwork was involved, the bureau in charge would present it directly, to reduce the burden of review and rejection.

sentences.zh: 初令五經諸書各置博士，國子學生員三十人。

translations.literal: For the first time doctors were appointed for each of the Five Classics and related books, with thirty students in the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Doctors were first appointed for each of the Five Classics and related texts, with thirty Imperial University students.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，置受恩、蒙養、長德、訓士四官。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of year 3, the four posts of Receiver of Grace, Nurtured in Honor, Upholder of Virtue, and Instructor of Scholars were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 3 the four posts Receiver of Grace, Nurtured in Honor, Upholder of Virtue, and Instructor of Scholars were created.

sentences.zh: 受恩職比特進，無常員，有人則置，親貴器望者為之。

translations.literal: Receiver of Grace ranked with Special Advancement, without fixed quota—when a man qualified, the post was filled, and it was held by those of close kinship, high rank, and established reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Receiver of Grace ranked with Special Advancement, without fixed quota—filled when a worthy man appeared—held by close kin of rank and established standing.

sentences.zh: 蒙養職比光祿大夫，無常員，取勤舊休閑者。

translations.literal: Nurtured in Honor ranked with Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, without fixed quota, drawn from those long in service who were now at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Nurtured in Honor ranked with Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, without fixed quota, given to veterans now in retirement.

sentences.zh: 長德職比中散大夫，無常員。

translations.literal: Upholder of Virtue ranked with Regular Palace Attendant, without fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Upholder of Virtue ranked with Regular Palace Attendant, without fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 訓士職比諫議大夫，規諷時政，匡刺非違。

translations.literal: Instructor of Scholars ranked with Grand Master of Remonstrance, admonishing current policy and correcting what was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Instructor of Scholars ranked with Grand Master of Remonstrance, to counsel on policy and correct abuses.

sentences.zh: 又置仙人博士官，典煮鍊百藥。

translations.literal: A Doctor of Immortals was also appointed to oversee the decoction and refining of all medicines.
translations.idiomatic: A Doctor of Immortals was also set up to supervise the preparation of all elixirs and drugs.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，罷匈奴中郎將官，令諸部護軍皆屬大將軍府。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of year 4, the post of Xiongnu Commandant was abolished, and all tribal Military Protectors were placed under the Grand General's office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 4 the Xiongnu Commandant was abolished and all tribal Military Protectors were subordinated to the Grand General's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 九月，罷外蘭臺御史，總屬內省。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Outer Orchid Terrace Censors were abolished and placed wholly under the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Outer Orchid Terrace censors were abolished and consolidated under the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十二月，復尚書三十六曹，曹置代人令史一人，譯令史一人，書令史二人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the thirty-six Secretariat bureaus were restored; each bureau was given one Di Ren Clerk, one Translation Clerk, and two Writing Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the thirty-six Secretariat bureaus were restored, each with one Di Ren clerk, one translation clerk, and two writing clerks.

sentences.zh: 天賜元年八月，初置六謁官，準古六卿，其秩五品。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Tianci [404], the six Petitioning Offices were first established, modeled on the ancient Six Ministers, of fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tianci year 1 (404) the six Petitioning Offices were first created, modeled on the ancient Six Ministers, at fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 屬官有大夫，秩六品。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials included grandees of sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates included grandees of sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 大夫屬官有元士，秩七品。

translations.literal: Under the grandees were Chief Gentlemen of seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under the grandees were Chief Gentlemen of seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 元士屬官有署令長，秩八品。

translations.literal: Under the Chief Gentlemen were Bureau Directors of eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Chief Gentlemen were bureau directors of eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 令長屬官有署丞，秩九品。

translations.literal: Under the directors were Bureau Assistants of ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under the directors were bureau assistants of ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 九月，減五等之爵，始分為四，曰王、公、侯、子，除伯、男二號。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the five grades of nobility were reduced; they were first divided into four, namely King, Duke, Marquis, and Viscount, and the titles Earl and Baron were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the five noble grades were cut to four—King, Duke, Marquis, and Viscount—and the titles Earl and Baron were dropped.

sentences.zh: 皇子及異姓元功上勳者封王，宗室及始蕃王皆降為公，諸公降為侯，侯、子亦以此為差。

translations.literal: Imperial sons and men of different surname with the highest merit and foremost achievement were enfeoffed as kings; members of the imperial clan and those first enfeoffed as kings were all reduced to dukes; all dukes were reduced to marquises; marquises and viscounts were reduced by the same scale.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sons and non-Tuoba men of supreme merit were enfeoffed as kings; imperial clansmen and those first made kings were demoted to dukes; dukes became marquises; marquises and viscounts were reduced in the same way.

sentences.zh: 於是封王者十人，公者二十二人，侯者七十九人，子者一百三人。

translations.literal: Thereupon ten were enfeoffed as kings, twenty-two as dukes, seventy-nine as marquises, and one hundred three as viscounts.
translations.idiomatic: Ten were then enfeoffed as kings, twenty-two as dukes, seventy-nine as marquises, and one hundred three as viscounts.

sentences.zh: 王封大郡，公封小郡，侯封大縣，子封小縣。

translations.literal: Kings received large commanderies, dukes small commanderies, marquises large counties, and viscounts small counties.
translations.idiomatic: Kings received large commanderies, dukes small commanderies, marquises large counties, and viscounts small counties.

sentences.zh: 王第一品，公第二品，侯第三品，子第四品。

translations.literal: Kings were first rank, dukes second rank, marquises third rank, and viscounts fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Kings ranked first grade, dukes second, marquises third, and viscounts fourth.

sentences.zh: 又制散官五等：五品散官比三都尉，六品散官比議郎，七品散官比太中、中散、諫議三大夫，八品散官比郎中，九品散官比舍人。

translations.literal: Dispersed offices were also regulated in five grades: fifth-rank dispersed offices equaled the Three Commandants; sixth-rank dispersed offices equaled Court Gentlemen; seventh-rank dispersed offices equaled the three grandees of Palace Attendant, Regular Palace Attendant, and Remonstrance; eighth-rank dispersed offices equaled Gentlemen of the Palace; ninth-rank dispersed offices equaled Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Dispersed offices were also set in five grades: fifth rank matched the Three Commandants; sixth rank matched Court Gentlemen; seventh rank matched the Grandees of the Palace, Regular Palace, and Remonstrance; eighth rank matched Gentlemen of the Palace; ninth rank matched Attendants.

sentences.zh: 文官五品已下，才能秀異者總比之造士，亦有五等。

translations.literal: For civil officials of fifth rank and below, those of outstanding talent were altogether compared to Advanced Scholars, also in five grades.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of fifth rank and below who showed outstanding talent were classed as Advanced Scholars, likewise in five grades.

sentences.zh: 武官五品已下堪任將帥者，亦有五等。

translations.literal: For military officials of fifth rank and below who were fit to serve as generals and commanders, there were also five grades.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials of fifth rank and below who were fit for command also had five grades.

sentences.zh: 若百官有闕者，則於中擢以補之。

translations.literal: Whenever any office in the hundred bureaus was vacant, men were selected from among these to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a regular post fell vacant, men were promoted from these pools to fill it.

sentences.zh: 初，帝欲法古純質，每於制定官號，多不依周漢舊名，或取諸身，或取諸物，或以民事，皆擬遠古雲鳥之義。

translations.literal: At first the emperor wished to follow the pure simplicity of antiquity; whenever he established official titles he often did not use the old names of Zhou and Han, but took them from the human body, from objects, or from civil affairs, all modeled on the meaning of clouds and birds in remote antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor sought the plain simplicity of antiquity; when devising titles he often avoided Zhou and Han names, drawing instead from the body, from things, or from civil life—all in the spirit of the cloud-and-bird offices of remote antiquity.

sentences.zh: 諸曹走使謂之鳧鴨，取飛之迅疾；

translations.literal: Runners of the various bureaus were called Wild Ducks, taking the swiftness of flight;
translations.idiomatic: Bureau runners were called Wild Ducks, for the speed of flight;

sentences.zh: 以伺察者為候官，謂之白鷺，取其延頸遠望。

translations.literal: those who conducted surveillance were made Surveillance Officers and called White Egrets, taking their long necks gazing into the distance.
translations.idiomatic: inspectors were Surveillance Officers called White Egrets, for craning the neck to see far.

sentences.zh: 自餘之官，義皆類此，咸有比況。

translations.literal: The remaining offices were all analogous in meaning, each with its comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Other offices followed the same pattern, each with its figurative basis.

sentences.zh: 又制諸州各置都尉以領兵。

translations.literal: It was also ordered that each province should appoint a Commandant to lead troops.
translations.idiomatic: Each province was also required to appoint a Commandant to command troops.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以八國姓族難分，故國立大師、小師，令辯其宗黨，品舉人才。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, because the clans of the Eight States were hard to distinguish, Great and Lesser Masters were established for the state, charged with clarifying lineages and grading and recommending talent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, because the Eight States' clans were hard to tell apart, Great and Lesser Masters were appointed to sort out lineages and grade talent for recommendation.

sentences.zh: 自八國以外，郡各自立師，職分如八國，比今之中正也。

translations.literal: Outside the Eight States each commandery likewise established masters, with duties like those of the Eight States, comparable to today's Rectifiers.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Eight States each commandery also appointed masters with the same duties—the equivalent of today's Rectifiers.

sentences.zh: 宗室立宗師，亦如州郡八國之儀。

translations.literal: For the imperial clan Clan Masters were established, following the same model as for the provinces, commanderies, and Eight States.
translations.idiomatic: For the imperial clan Clan Masters were appointed on the same model as in the provinces, commanderies, and Eight States.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔始賜王、公、侯、子國臣吏，大郡王二百人，次郡王、上郡公百人，次郡公五十人，侯二十五人，子十二人，皆立典師，職比家丞，總統羣隸。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month an edict first granted kings, dukes, marquises, and viscounts retainers for their states: kings of large commanderies two hundred men, kings of secondary commanderies and dukes of superior commanderies one hundred, dukes of secondary commanderies fifty, marquises twenty-five, and viscounts twelve; each establishment had a Director Master, ranking like a Household Chancellor, to oversee all subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month an edict first allotted retainers to enfeoffed kings, dukes, marquises, and viscounts: two hundred for kings of large commanderies, one hundred for lesser kings and dukes of superior commanderies, fifty for dukes of lesser commanderies, twenty-five for marquises, and twelve for viscounts—each with a Director Master ranking like a household chancellor to supervise all staff.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，復罷尚書三十六曹，別置武歸、修勤二職。

translations.literal: In the second month of year 2 the thirty-six Secretariat bureaus were again abolished, and the separate posts of Martial Return and Diligent Service were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 2 the thirty-six Secretariat bureaus were abolished again, and the separate posts Martial Return and Diligent Service were created.

sentences.zh: 武歸比郎中，修勤比令史，分主省務。

translations.literal: Martial Return ranked with Gentlemen of the Palace and Diligent Service with Clerks, dividing supervision of secretariat affairs between them.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Return ranked with Gentlemen of the Palace and Diligent Service with clerks, dividing secretariat duties between them.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，[2]置內官員二十人，比侍中、常侍，迭直左右。

translations.literal: [2] In the first month of year 2 twenty Inner Officials were appointed, ranking with Palace Attendants and Regular Attendants, serving in rotation at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: [2] In the first month of year 2 twenty Inner Officials were appointed, ranking with Palace and Regular Attendants, rotating duty at the ruler's side.

sentences.zh: 又制諸州置三刺史，刺史用品第六者，宗室一人，異姓二人，比古之上中下三大夫也。

translations.literal: It was also ordered that each province should have three Inspectors, Inspectors of sixth-rank salary: one from the imperial clan and two of different surname, comparable to the ancient Greater, Middle, and Lesser Grand Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Each province was also to have three Inspectors of sixth-rank salary—one imperial clansman and two of other surnames—like the ancient Greater, Middle, and Lesser Grandees.

sentences.zh: 郡置三太守，用七品者。

translations.literal: Each commandery had three Grand Administrators drawn from seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each commandery had three Grand Administrators of seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 縣置三令長，八品者。

translations.literal: Each county had three Magistrates of eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each county had three magistrates of eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 刺史、令長各之州縣，以太守上有刺史，下有令長，雖置而未臨民。

translations.literal: Inspectors and magistrates each went to their provinces and counties; above the Grand Administrator were Inspectors and below him magistrates—though appointed, they did not yet govern the people directly.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors and magistrates went to their posts; above the Grand Administrator stood the Inspectors and below him the magistrates—appointed, but not yet administering the people directly.

sentences.zh: 自前功臣為州者徵還京師，以爵歸第。

translations.literal: Former meritorious officials who had served as provincial governors were summoned back to the capital and retired to their estates with their titles.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious officials who had previously governed provinces were recalled to the capital and retired to their estates with their titles.

sentences.zh: 置散騎郎、獵郎、諸省令史、省事、典籤等。

translations.literal: Regular Attendants of the Fast Steed, Hunting Gentlemen, clerks of the various secretariats, Office Attendants, Registry Masters, and the like were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Attendants of the Fast Steed, Hunting Gentlemen, secretariat clerks, office attendants, registry masters, and the like were appointed.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，增置侍官，侍直左右，出內詔命，取八國良家，代郡、上谷、廣寧、雁門四郡民中年長有器望者充之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of year 4 Attendant Officials were increased; they attended on duty at the ruler's side and issued inner edicts, chosen from good families of the Eight States and from men of mature years with standing and reputation among the people of the four commanderies of Dai, Shanggu, Guangning, and Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 4 more Attendant Officials were added to stand duty at the ruler's side and issue inner edicts, drawn from reputable families of the Eight States and from mature, respected men of Dai, Shanggu, Guangning, and Yanmen commanderies.

sentences.zh: 永興元年十一月，置騏驎官四十人，宿直殿省，比常侍、侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Yongxing [413], forty Qilin Officials were appointed to lodge on duty in the palace offices, ranking with Regular Attendants and Gentlemen Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Yongxing year 1 (413) forty Qilin Officials were appointed for night duty in the palace, ranking with Regular and Gentlemen Attendants.

sentences.zh: 神瑞元年春，置八大人官，大人下置三屬官，總理萬機，故世號八公云。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Shenrui [414], the eight Chief posts were established; under each Chief three subordinate officials were placed, administering all affairs of state, and so they were called the Eight Dukes in their time.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Shenrui year 1 (414) the eight Chief posts were created, each with three subordinates, to manage all state affairs—hence they were known as the Eight Dukes.

sentences.zh: 泰常二年夏，置六部大人官，有天部，地部，東、西、南、北部，皆以諸公為之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Taichang [417], the six Division Chief posts were established: Heaven Division, Earth Division, and Eastern, Western, Southern, and Northern Divisions, all filled by dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Taichang year 2 (417) six Division Chiefs were appointed—for Heaven, Earth, and the Eastern, Western, Southern, and Northern divisions—all held by dukes.

sentences.zh: 大人置三屬官。

translations.literal: Each Chief had three subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: Each Chief had three subordinate officials.

sentences.zh: 始光元年正月，置右民尚書。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Shiguang [424], the Right Minister of the People was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Shiguang year 1 (424) the Right Minister of the People was appointed.

sentences.zh: 七月，詔諸征鎮大將依品開府，以置佐吏。

translations.literal: In the seventh month an edict ordered that all campaigning and garrison grand generals should open offices according to rank in order to appoint staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month an edict directed all campaigning and garrison grand generals to open headquarters according to rank and appoint staff.

sentences.zh: 延和元年三月，改代尹為萬年尹，代令為萬年令。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Yanhe [432], the Governor of Dai was renamed Governor of Wannian and the Magistrate of Dai Magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yanhe year 1 (432) the Governor of Dai was renamed Governor of Wannian and the Magistrate of Dai Magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 後復。

translations.literal: Later the old names were restored.
translations.idiomatic: The old names were later restored.

sentences.zh: 真君五年正月，侍中、中書監、宜都王穆壽，司徒、東郡公崔浩，侍中、廣平公張黎輔政，置通事四人。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year of Zhenjun [444], Palace Attendant and Supervisor of the Secretariat Mu Shou, King of Yidu, Grand Tutor Cui Hao, Duke of Dongjun, and Palace Attendant Zhang Li, Duke of Guangping, assisted in government, and four Communications Officers were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhenjun year 5 (444) Palace Attendant and Secretariat Supervisor Mu Shou, King of Yidu, Grand Tutor Cui Hao, Duke of Dongjun, and Palace Attendant Zhang Li, Duke of Guangping, formed the regency council, and four Communications Officers were appointed.

sentences.zh: 又選諸曹良吏，給事東宮。

translations.literal: Able clerks from the various bureaus were also selected to serve in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Able clerks from the bureaus were also chosen to serve in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 興安二年正月，置駕部尚書、右士尚書。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Xing'an [453], the Ministers of the Imperial Carriage Department and Right Minister of the Gentlemen were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xing'an year 2 (453) the Ministers of the Imperial Carriage Department and Right Minister of the Gentlemen were appointed.

sentences.zh: 太安三年五月，以諸部護軍各為太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Tai'an [457], all tribal Military Protectors were made Grand Administrators.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tai'an year 3 (457) all tribal Military Protectors were made Grand Administrators.

sentences.zh: 延興二年五月，詔曰：「非功無以受爵，非能無以受祿，凡出外遷者皆引此奏聞，求乞假品。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Yanxing [472] an edict said: "Without merit one may not receive a noble title, and without ability one may not receive salary. All who are transferred to posts outside the capital must cite this in memorials to the throne when seeking provisional ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yanxing year 2 (472) an edict declared: "Without merit there is no noble title, and without ability no salary. All officials transferred to posts outside the capital must cite this when memorializing for provisional ranks.

sentences.zh: 在職有效，聽下附正，若無殊稱，隨而削之。

translations.literal: If effective in office, they might on leaving have the provisional rank attached to the regular one; if they had no special distinction, it was reduced accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: If they performed well in office, on departure the provisional rank could be made permanent; without special merit, it was reduced or withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 舊制諸鎮將、刺史假五等爵，及有所貢獻而得假爵者，皆不得世襲。」

translations.literal: By the old regulation, provisional noble titles of the five grades granted to garrison generals and inspectors, and provisional titles obtained through tribute, could none of them be inherited."
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, provisional noble titles of the five grades granted to garrison generals and inspectors, and titles obtained through tribute, could not be inherited."

sentences.zh: 四年二月，置外牧官。

translations.literal: In the second month of year 4, Outer Herd Officials were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 4 Outer Herd Officials were appointed.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，置監御曹。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of year 5, the Supervisory Imperial Bureau was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 5 the Supervisory Imperial Bureau was established.

sentences.zh: 太和二年五月，減置候職四百人，司察非違。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Taihe [478], four hundred Surveillance posts were reduced and established, charged with investigating violations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Taihe year 2 (478) four hundred surveillance posts were cut to size and charged with investigating misconduct.

sentences.zh: 四年，省二部內部幢將。

translations.literal: In year 4 the Banner Generals of the inner divisions of the two Departments were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the inner Banner Generals of the two divisions were abolished.

sentences.zh: 十一年八月，置散官員一百人，朝請員二百人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of year 11, one hundred Dispersed Officials and two hundred Court Petitioners were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 11 one hundred Dispersed Officials and two hundred Court Petitioners were appointed.

sentences.zh: 十五年七月，置司儀官。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of year 15, Masters of Ceremonies were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 15 Masters of Ceremonies were appointed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，置侍中、黃門各四人，又置散騎常侍、侍郎，員各四人；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, four Palace Attendants and four Yellow Gate Attendants were appointed, and also four Regular Attendants of the Fast Steed and four Gentlemen Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month four Palace Attendants and four Yellow Gate Attendants were appointed, along with four Regular Attendants of the Fast Steed and four Gentlemen Attendants;

sentences.zh: 通直散騎常侍、侍郎，員外散騎常侍、侍郎，各六人。

translations.literal: six Unrestricted Regular Attendants of the Fast Steed and Gentlemen Attendants, and six Regular Attendants of the Fast Steed and Gentlemen Attendants Outside the Regular Quota.
translations.idiomatic: six Unrestricted Regular and Gentlemen Attendants of the Fast Steed, and six Outside-the-Quota Regular and Gentlemen Attendants of the Fast Steed.

sentences.zh: 又置司空、主客、太倉、庫部、都牧、太樂、虞曹、宮輿、覆育少卿官。

translations.literal: Assistant Ministers were also appointed for the Minister of Works, Master of Guests, Grand Storehouse, Treasury Bureau, Chief Herds, Grand Music, Parks Bureau, Palace Carriages, and Nurturing the Young.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant ministers were also appointed for Works, Guests, the Grand Storehouse, Treasury, Chief Herds, Grand Music, Parks, Palace Carriages, and Nurturing the Young.

sentences.zh: 又置光爵、驍游、五校、中大夫、散員士官。

translations.literal: Officers of Radiant Nobility, Valiant Rovers, the Five Commandants, Middle Grand Masters, and Dispersed Staff were also appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Officers of Radiant Nobility, Valiant Rovers, the Five Commandants, Middle Grandees, and Dispersed Staff were also appointed.

sentences.zh: 又置侍官一百二十人。

translations.literal: One hundred twenty Attendant Officials were also appointed.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred twenty Attendant Officials were also appointed.

sentences.zh: 改立諸局監羽林、虎賁。

translations.literal: The various bureau directors over the Forest of Cavalry and the Tiger Guard were changed and re-established.
translations.idiomatic: The directors of the bureaus overseeing the Forest of Cavalry and the Tiger Guard were reorganized.

sentences.zh: 舊制，諸以勳賜官爵者子孫世襲軍號。

translations.literal: Under the old system, for all those granted offices and noble ranks for merit, their descendants inherited military titles in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, the descendants of men granted offices and noble titles for meritorious service inherited military ranks from generation to generation.

sentences.zh: 十六年，改降五等，始革之，止襲爵而已。

translations.literal: In year 16, when the five grades were changed and reduced, this was first abolished; only noble titles could be inherited.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16, when the five noble grades were restructured, the practice was abolished—only hereditary noble titles remained.

sentences.zh: 舊制，緣邊皆置鎮都大將，統兵備禦，與刺史同。

translations.literal: Under the old system, along the frontiers garrison commanders-in-chief were all appointed, commanding troops for defense, ranking equal to Inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, every frontier region had a garrison commander-in-chief who commanded troops for defense and ranked on a par with a provincial inspector.

sentences.zh: 城隍、倉庫皆鎮將主之，但不治。

translations.literal: City walls and moats and storehouses were all presided over by garrison generals, but they did not administer civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison generals held authority over city fortifications and storehouses, but did not govern the civilian population.

sentences.zh: 故為重於刺史。

translations.literal: Therefore they were regarded as heavier than Inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they outranked provincial inspectors in importance.

translations.idiomatic: 〈Doubtful passage in the transmitted text.〉

translations.idiomatic: [3] (Note: The text likely omits the word for "the people" after "did not administer"; missing material below makes the passage unclear.)

sentences.zh: 自太祖至高祖初，其內外百官屢有減置，或事出當時，不為常目，如萬騎、飛鴻、常忠、直意將軍之徒是也。

translations.literal: From Emperor Taizu down to the early reign of Emperor Gaozu, the inner and outer officials were repeatedly reduced or established; some posts arose from the needs of the moment and were not part of the regular roster, such as the Generals of Ten Thousand Riders, Flying Swan, Constant Loyalty, and Direct Intent.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Taizu to the early years of Emperor Xiaowen, civil and military offices were repeatedly added or cut; some were ad hoc appointments, not part of the permanent table—such as the Generals of Ten Thousand Riders, Flying Swan, Constant Loyalty, and Direct Intent.

sentences.zh: 舊令亡失，無所依據。

translations.literal: The old regulations were lost and destroyed, and there was nothing on which to rely.
translations.idiomatic: The old regulations had been lost, leaving no authority to cite.

sentences.zh: 太和中高祖詔羣僚議定百官，著於令，今列於左，勳品、流外位卑而不載矣。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era Emperor Gaozu ordered the assembled officials to deliberate and fix the hundred offices, recording them in the regulations; they are now listed at left, while ranks of merit and extra-bureaucratic posts too low in rank are not entered.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe reign Emperor Xiaowen ordered his ministers to settle the official hierarchy and codify it in statute; that table is listed below. Ranks of merit and positions outside the regular bureaucracy, being too low in rank, are omitted.

sentences.zh: 十九年八月，初置直齋、御仗左右武官。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of year 19, the Direct-Fast officers and left and right martial officers of the imperial guard were first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 19 the Direct-Fast officers and left and right martial officers of the imperial guard were first created.

translations.literal: [8] (Editor's note: On "first establishing the Direct-Fast officers and left and right martial officers of the imperial guard": various editions mistakenly read "Qi" for "Direct-Fast"; the Imperial Readings, juan 240, reads "Direct-Fast." Biography of Erzhu Shilong in juan 75 says, "At the end of Emperor Suzong's reign he served as Direct-Fast officer, then transferred to Direct-Quarters officer, later concurrently Direct-Pavilion officer"; Annals of Emperor Chu in juan 111, fifth month, bingxu day of Yongxi year 3, says, "Cavalry officers ranked equal to Direct-Fast officers." Tongdian juan 38 gives Northern Qi official ranks with Direct-Quarters and Direct-Fast at subordinate fifth rank, which should follow Wei practice. Here one character was confused for another; the text is corrected accordingly.)
translations.idiomatic: [8] (Note: For "first establishing Direct-Fast officers and imperial-guard left and right martial officers," some editions miswrite one form for another; Imperial Readings j. 240 has the correct reading. Shilong's biography (j. 75) and the Chu emperor annals (j. 111) treat Direct-Fast as a recognized post; Tongdian j. 38 places Direct-Fast at subordinate fifth rank under Northern Qi, following Wei practice. The error is emended.)

sentences.zh: 二十三年，高祖復次職令，及帝崩，世宗初班行之，以為永制。

translations.literal: In year 23, Emperor Gaozu again ordered the official regulations by rank; when the emperor died, at the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign they were first promulgated and made a permanent system.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 Emperor Xiaowen revised the rank regulations again; after his death, Emperor Xuanwu promulgated them at the start of his reign and made them the permanent order.

sentences.zh: 右從第九品

translations.literal: Above: Subordinate Ninth Rank
translations.idiomatic: (Subordinate ninth rank)

sentences.zh: 前世職次皆無從品，魏氏始置之，亦一代之別制也。

translations.literal: In previous ages official grades had no subordinate ranks; the Wei first established them—it was also a distinctive institution of that generation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynasties had no subordinate ranks within a grade; the Wei were the first to institute them—a peculiarity of their age.

sentences.zh: 正始元年十一月，罷郡中正。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Zhengshi year 1, the commandery impartial selectors were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first Zhengshi year, commandery impartial selectors were abolished.

sentences.zh: 四年九月詔曰：「五校昔統營位，次於列卿，奉車都尉禁侍美官，顯加通貴。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of year 4 an edict said: "The Five Commandants once commanded encampments, ranking below the column of ministers; the Commandant Who Attends the Chariot was a restricted, favored post, conspicuously elevated and privileged.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 4 an edict declared: "The Five Commandants once commanded camp garrisons and ranked just below the ministers; the Commandant of the Chariot of State was a restricted court of honor, markedly elevated and privileged.

sentences.zh: 世移時變，遂為冗職。

translations.literal: Times changed, and they became supernumerary posts.
translations.idiomatic: As the times shifted, they became hollow titles.

sentences.zh: 既典名猶昔，宜有定員，并殿中二司馬亦須有常數。

translations.literal: Since their titles remain as of old, fixed quotas ought to be set; the two Palace Army Supervisors also need regular numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Their names still carry old prestige, so each should have a fixed quota—including the two Palace Army Supervisors.

sentences.zh: 今五校可各二十人，奉車都尉二十人，騎都尉六十人，殿中司馬二百人，員外司馬三百人。」

translations.literal: Let each of the Five Commandants now have twenty men; the Commandant Who Attends the Chariot twenty; the Commandant of Cavalry sixty; Palace Army Supervisors two hundred; Outside-the-Quota Army Supervisors three hundred."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth let each of the Five Commandants have twenty posts; the Commandant of the Chariot of State twenty; the Commandant of Cavalry sixty; Palace Army Supervisors two hundred; and Outside-the-Quota Army Supervisors three hundred."

sentences.zh: 永平元年十二月，尚書令高肇，尚書僕射、清河王懌等奏置小學博士員三千人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of Yongping year 1, Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Zhao, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi, and others memorialized to establish three thousand Primary School erudite posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first Yongping year, Minister of State Affairs Gao Zhao, Vice Minister and Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi, and others memorialized to set the Primary School erudite quota at three thousand.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，尚書令高肇奏，都水臺請依舊二使者，參軍事、謁者并錄事、令史亦隨事更立。

translations.literal: In the first month of year 2, Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Zhao memorialized that the Directorate of Waterways requested, as in the old arrangement, two commissioners, and that staff attendants, ushers, recorders, and chief clerks also be re-established as needed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 2, Minister Gao Zhao memorialized that the Directorate of Waterways asked to restore the former two commissioners and to re-establish staff attendants, ushers, recorders, and chief clerks as required.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「使者置二，可如所奏。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Let two commissioners be appointed, as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "Appoint two commissioners, as requested.

sentences.zh: 其下屬司，唯須充事耳，亦何勞多也。

translations.literal: Their subordinate offices need only be filled for service—why trouble over so many posts?
translations.idiomatic: The offices beneath them need only be staffed for the work—what need for so many?

sentences.zh: 參軍、錄事並更置一，謁者加二，令史依舊。」

translations.literal: Appoint one more staff attendant and recorder each; add two ushers; keep chief clerks as before."
translations.idiomatic: Add one staff attendant and one recorder; increase ushers by two; leave chief clerks unchanged."

sentences.zh: 肇又奏諸州諮議、記室、戶曹、刑獄、田曹、水曹、集曹、士曹參軍悉併省之。

translations.literal: Zhao further memorialized that advisory, recording, household, punishment, field, water, collection, and scholar staff attendants in all provinces be consolidated and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao further proposed abolishing and merging the provincial advisory, recording, household, punishment, field, water, collection, and scholar staff attendants.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，詔改宗子羽林為宗士，其本秩付尚書計其資集，敍從七已下、從八已上官。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of year 4, an edict changed the Clan Cadet Forest of Cavalry to Clan Scholars; their original ranks were turned over to the Masters of Writing to calculate seniority, and they were promoted to offices from subordinate seventh rank downward through subordinate eighth rank upward.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 4, an edict renamed the Clan Cadet Forest of Cavalry as Clan Scholars; the Masters of Writing were to calculate their seniority from their former ranks and promote them to posts from subordinate seventh rank down through subordinate eighth rank up.

sentences.zh: 正光元年七月，置左、右衞將軍各二人。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Zhengguang year 1, Left and Right Guard Generals were established, two each.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first Zhengguang year, two Left Guard Generals and two Right Guard Generals were appointed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，罷諸州中正，郡縣定姓族，後復。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the provincial impartial selectors were abolished and commanderies and districts fixed clan registers; the office was later restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month provincial impartial selectors were abolished and commanderies and districts were ordered to fix clan registers; the office was later restored.

sentences.zh: 孝昌二年十月，詔宗士、庶子二官各增二百人。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Xiaochang year 2, an edict increased the Clan Scholar and Attendant posts by two hundred each.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second Xiaochang year, an edict added two hundred posts each to the Clan Scholar and Attendant offices.

sentences.zh: 置望士隊四百人，取肺腑之族有武藝者。

translations.literal: A Gazing Scholar company of four hundred was established, drawn from close imperial kin with martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: A four-hundred-man Gazing Scholar company was formed, recruited from imperial relatives with martial ability.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，以尒朱榮有扶翼之功，拜柱國大將軍，位在丞相上；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, because Erzhu Rong had the merit of supporting the throne, he was appointed Pillar-of-State Grand General, ranking above the Chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, Erzhu Rong was appointed Pillar-of-State Grand General for his service in raising the throne, ranking above the Chancellor;

sentences.zh: 又拜大丞相、天柱大將軍，增佐吏。

translations.literal: He was also appointed Grand Chancellor and Pillar-of-Heaven Grand General, with additional staff increased.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Grand Chancellor and Pillar-of-Heaven Grand General, with an enlarged staff.

sentences.zh: 又以太尉、上黨王天穆為太宰，增佐吏。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant and Prince of Shangdang Tian Mu was also appointed Grand Preceptor, with additional staff increased.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant and Prince of Shangdang Tian Mu was likewise appointed Grand Preceptor, with an enlarged staff.

sentences.zh: 永安二年各詔復置司直十人，視五品，隸廷尉，覆治御史檢劾事。

translations.literal: In the second Yongan year separate edicts restored ten Direct Investigators, treated as fifth rank, subordinate to the Minister of Justice, to review cases investigated by the censors.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Yongan year separate edicts restored ten Direct Investigators, ranked as fifth grade, under the Minister of Punishments, to re-examine cases the censors had investigated.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，以尒朱世隆為儀同三師，位次上公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, Erzhu Shilong was appointed Three Preceptors of Equal Privilege, ranking below the upper dukes.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Putai, Erzhu Shilong was made Three Preceptors of Equal Privilege, ranking just below the senior dukes.

sentences.zh: 又侍中、黃門、武衞將軍，並增置六人。

translations.literal: Palace Attendants, Yellow Gate Attendants, and Martial Guard Generals were also each increased by six posts.
translations.idiomatic: Six additional posts were also created for Palace Attendants, Yellow Gate Attendants, and Martial Guard Generals.

sentences.zh: 永安已後，遠近多事，置京畿大都督，復立州都督，俱總軍人。

translations.literal: After Yongan, with turmoil near and far, a Metropolitan Area Grand Commander was appointed, and provincial commanders were re-established; both commanded troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongan, as trouble spread near and far, a Metropolitan Area Grand Commander was appointed and provincial commanders were restored; both oversaw military forces.

sentences.zh: 天平四年夏，罷六州都督，悉隸京畿，其京畿大都督仍不改焉。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth Tianping year, the six provincial commanders were abolished and all were subordinated to the metropolitan area; the Metropolitan Area Grand Commander remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Tianping year 4, the six provincial commanders were abolished and placed under the metropolitan command; the Metropolitan Area Grand Commander remained as before.

sentences.zh: 立府置佐。

translations.literal: Headquarters were established and staff appointed.
translations.idiomatic: A headquarters was set up with a full staff.

sentences.zh: 舊制：有大將軍，不置太尉；

translations.literal: Under the old rule: when there was a Grand General, no Grand Commandant was appointed;
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, if a Grand General held office, no Grand Commandant was appointed;

sentences.zh: 有丞相，不置司徒。

translations.literal: When there was a Chancellor, no Minister over the Masses was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: If a Chancellor held office, no Minister of Education was appointed.

sentences.zh: 自正光已後，天下多事，勳賢並軌，乃俱置之。

translations.literal: From Zhengguang onward, with turmoil throughout the realm and many meritorious men of rank side by side, both were appointed together.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhengguang onward the realm was in constant turmoil and meritorious men crowded the highest ranks, so both posts were filled at once.

sentences.zh: 武定二年十一月，有司奏：「齊獻武王勳高德重，禮絕羣辟。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Wuding year 2, the relevant offices memorialized: "The Meritorious and Virtuous Prince of Qi, Gao Huan, ranks above the host of ministers by merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Wuding year 2, the relevant offices memorialized: "Prince of Qi Gao Huan, meritorious and virtuous, stands above the assembled ministers in honor.

sentences.zh: 昔霍光陵邑亦置長、丞主陵，今請置長一人，丞一人，錄事一人，戶曹史一人，禁備史一人，侍一人，皆降帝陵官品一等。

translations.literal: When Huo Guang's tomb precinct was established, a director and assistant director were also appointed to administer the tomb; we now request one director, one assistant director, one recorder, one household officer clerk, one guard-recorder clerk, and one attendant, all one grade below imperial tomb officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Huo Guang's tomb precinct was established, a director and assistant were appointed to tend the tomb; we ask now for one director, one assistant director, one recorder, one household clerk, one guard-recorder clerk, and one attendant, each one grade below imperial tomb officials.

sentences.zh: 其侍依舊。」

translations.literal: The attendant should follow the old arrangement."
translations.idiomatic: The attendant should remain as before.

sentences.zh: 詔「可」。

translations.literal: The edict replied: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered: "Granted."

sentences.zh: 七年三月，詔左右光祿大夫各置二人，金紫光祿大夫置四人，光祿大夫置四人，太中、中散各置六人。

translations.literal: In the third month of year 7, an edict ordered that Left and Right Supervisors of Grand Masters of Splendor each have two posts established, that four posts of Grand Master of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon be established, that four posts of Grand Master of Splendor be established, and that Grand Masters of Palace and Regular Attendants each have six posts established.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year, an edict fixed the establishment at two each for the Left and Right Supervisors of Grandees of Splendor, four for Grandees of Splendor with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, four for Grandees of Splendor, and six each for Grandees of Palace and Regular Attendants.

sentences.zh: 五月，又詔以四中郎將，世宗永平中權隸領軍，今還屬護軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, another edict placed the four Central Commandants—who during Emperor Shizong's Yongping reign had been temporarily subordinate to the Director of the Army—back under the Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, another edict returned the four Central Commandants to the Protector of the Army; during Emperor Shizong's Yongping era they had provisionally been assigned to the Director of the Army.

sentences.zh: 自古天子立德，因生以賜姓，胙之土而命之氏；

translations.literal: From antiquity the Son of Heaven established virtue; according to birth he bestowed surnames, and by granting fief lands he assigned clan names.
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times emperors have established virtue by bestowing surnames according to birth and assigning clan names when granting fief lands.

sentences.zh: 諸侯則以家與諡，官有世功，則有宦族，邑亦如之。

translations.literal: Feudal lords likewise took names from their houses and posthumous titles; when officials had hereditary merit, there were official clans, and fiefs worked the same way.
translations.idiomatic: For feudal lords, names came from family and posthumous titles; officials with hereditary service formed official clans, and the same principle applied to fiefholders.

sentences.zh: 姓則表其所由生，氏則記族所由出，其大略然也。

translations.literal: The surname indicates the source of one's birth; the clan name records the origin from which the lineage emerged—such is the general principle.
translations.idiomatic: A surname marks where one was born into the world; a clan name records the lineage's origin—that is the broad pattern.

sentences.zh: 至於或自所居，或以國號，或用官爵，或用事物，雖緣時不同，俱其義矣。

translations.literal: As for deriving names from one's dwelling place, or from a state title, or from office and rank, or from objects and affairs—though the occasions differ, the principle is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a name came from a place of residence, a state designation, an office and rank, or some object or event, the custom varied with the times but the logic was the same.

sentences.zh: 魏氏本居朔壤，地遠俗殊，賜姓命氏，其事不一，亦如長勺、尾氏、終葵之屬也。

translations.literal: The Wei originally dwelt in the northern frontier; the land was remote and customs differed, and the bestowal of surnames and assignment of clan names were not uniform, just like clans such as Changshao, Wei, and Zhongkui.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei people originally lived in the northern marches, where distance and custom made surname-granting and clan-naming less uniform—as with such names as Changshao, Wei, and Zhongkui.

sentences.zh: 初，安帝統國，諸部有九十九姓。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Emperor An unified the state, the various tribes had ninety-nine surnames.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor An first unified the realm, the tribes counted ninety-nine surnames among them.

sentences.zh: 至獻帝時，七分國人，使諸兄弟各攝領之，乃分其氏。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Xian, the people of the state were divided into seven parts, each of his brothers placed in charge of one, and their clans were thereby separated.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xian the people were split seven ways, each brother given a share to govern, and the clans were divided accordingly.

sentences.zh: 自後兼并他國，各有本部，部中別族，為內姓焉。

translations.literal: Afterward, as other states were annexed, each had its own original tribe; subsidiary clans within the tribes became the inner surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as other peoples were absorbed, each kept its original tribal affiliation, with sub-clans within the tribes forming the inner surnames.

sentences.zh: 年世稍久，互以改易，興衰存滅，間有之矣，今舉其可知者。

translations.literal: As years passed, names were changed back and forth; rise and fall, survival and extinction occurred occasionally; what can still be known is listed here.
translations.idiomatic: Over time names were altered repeatedly, with some clans rising, falling, surviving, or disappearing; here are those that can still be traced.

sentences.zh: 獻帝以兄為紇骨氏，後改為胡氏。

sentences.zh: 凡與帝室為十姓，百世不通婚。

translations.literal: In all, together with the imperial house there were ten clans; for a hundred generations they did not intermarry.
translations.idiomatic: Ten clans in all, including the imperial line, were forbidden to intermarry for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 太和以前，國之喪葬祠禮，非十族不得與也。

translations.literal: Before the Taihe era, in the state's mourning, burial, and sacrificial rites, only the ten clans might participate.
translations.idiomatic: Until the Taihe reforms, only members of the ten clans could take part in state funerals and sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 高祖革之，各以職司從事。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu reformed this; each clan participated according to its official duties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu abolished that restriction; each clan took part according to its rank and office.

sentences.zh: 神元皇帝時，餘部諸姓內入者。

translations.literal: During Emperor Shenyuan, the remaining tribes whose surnames entered the inner register.

translations.idiomatic: Duguhun was later Sinicized as Du.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸部，其渠長皆自統眾，而尉遲已下不及賀蘭諸部氏。

translations.literal: Of all these divisions, their chiefs each commanded their own followers on their own, but from Yuchi downward they did not match the clans of the Helan divisions.
translations.idiomatic: All these divisions had chiefs who led their own people, but from Yuchi down they were less eminent than the Helan clans.

sentences.zh: 北方賀蘭，後改為賀氏。

translations.literal: In the North, Helan; later it was changed to the He clan.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Helan was later shortened to He.

sentences.zh: 郁都甄氏，後改為甄氏。

translations.literal: The Yuduzhen clan; later it was changed to the Zhen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuduzhen was later shortened to Zhen.

translations.idiomatic: [41] Editorial note marker in the source text.

translations.literal: The Hexi clan; later it was changed to the Ji clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi was later Sinicized as Ji.

sentences.zh: 越勒氏，後改為越氏。

translations.literal: The Yuele clan; later it was changed to the Yue clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuele was later shortened to Yue.

translations.idiomatic: [42] Editorial note marker in the source text.

translations.literal: The Chinu clan; later it was changed to the Lang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Chinu was later Sinicized as Lang.

sentences.zh: 渴燭渾氏，後改為味氏。

translations.literal: The Kezhuhun clan; later it was changed to the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhuhun was later Sinicized as Wei.

translations.literal: Editorial commentary marker [43] stands here in the transmitted text.
translations.idiomatic: [43] Editorial note marker in the source text.

sentences.zh: 庫褥官氏，後改為庫氏。

translations.literal: The Kuruguan clan; later it was changed to the Ku clan.
translations.idiomatic: Kuruguan was later shortened to Ku.

sentences.zh: 烏洛蘭氏，後為蘭氏。

translations.literal: The Wuluolan clan; later it became the Lan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wuluolan later became Lan.

sentences.zh: 一那蔞氏，後改為蔞氏。

translations.literal: The Yinalou clan; later it was changed to the Lou clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yinalou was later shortened to Lou.

sentences.zh: 羽弗氏，後改為羽氏。

translations.literal: The Yufu clan; later it was changed to the Yu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yufu was later shortened to Yu.

sentences.zh: 凡此四方諸部，歲時朝貢，登國初，太祖散諸部落，始同為編民。

translations.literal: All these divisions of the four directions paid seasonal tribute; at the beginning of the Dengguo reign, Taizu dispersed the various tribes, and they first became registered commoners alike.
translations.idiomatic: These divisions of east, west, south, and north paid tribute at the seasons; early in the Dengguo era Taizu broke up the tribal encampments, and all alike became registered subjects.

sentences.zh: 太和十九年，詔曰：「代人諸冑，先無姓族，雖功賢之胤，混然未分。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Taihe, an edict said: "Among the various scions of the conqueror clans, there were originally no surnamed lineages; even descendants of meritorious and worthy men were mixed together and undifferentiated.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 19 (495), an edict stated: "The conqueror clans had no formal surname lineages; even the heirs of men of merit and talent remained undistinguished in one undifferentiated mass.

sentences.zh: 故官達者位極公卿，其功衰之親，仍居猥任。

translations.literal: Thus those who attained office rose to the rank of Duke and Minister, while their kinsmen whose merit had faded still held menial posts.
translations.idiomatic: Those who rose high reached the highest offices, yet relatives whose families' distinction had waned still languished in low posts.

sentences.zh: 比欲制定姓族，事多未就，且宜甄擢，隨時漸銓。

translations.literal: As we now wish to establish surname lineages, much of the work is still unfinished; for the present we should select and promote men, gradually assessing them as time allows.
translations.idiomatic: We mean to fix surname rankings, but the work is far from complete; for now, select the worthy and advance them step by step.

sentences.zh: 其穆、陸、賀、劉、樓、于、嵇、尉八姓，皆太祖已降，勳著當世，位盡王公；

translations.literal: As for the eight surnames Mu, Lu, He, Liu, Lou, Yu, Ji, and Yu—they are all since Taizu's time, their merit conspicuous in the age, their offices all reaching King and Duke;
translations.idiomatic: The eight surnames Mu, Lu, He, Liu, Lou, Yu, Ji, and Yu—all families of distinction since Taizu, famed in their day, with ranks reaching king and duke—

sentences.zh: 灼然可知者，且下司州、吏部勿充猥官，一同四姓。

translations.literal: those clearly ascertainable shall not be assigned to menial posts by the Sizhou or Ministry of Personnel, but treated the same as the four surname lineages.
translations.idiomatic: where this is unmistakable, the Ministry of Personnel and Sizhou shall not fill them into base offices, but treat them on a par with the four surname clans.

sentences.zh: 自此以外，應班士流者，尋續別敕。

translations.literal: Beyond this, those who should be ranked among the gentry will receive separate edicts in due course.
translations.idiomatic: All others who merit gentry standing will be addressed in separate orders to follow.

sentences.zh: 原出朔土，舊為部落大人，而自皇始已來，有三世官在給事已上，及州刺史、鎮大將，及品登王公者為姓。

translations.literal: Those originally from the northern frontier who were formerly tribal great chiefs, and since Huangshi have had three generations holding office at Attendant within the Yellow Gate and above, or as prefect of a province or General-in-chief of a garrison, or whose rank reaches King or Duke, are designated surnamed lineages.
translations.idiomatic: Men of northern origin who were once tribal chiefs, and since Huangshi have held office for three generations at Attendant within the Yellow Gate or higher, or as provincial prefect, garrison commander-in-chief, or with rank reaching king or duke, qualify as surnamed lineages.

sentences.zh: 若本非大人，而皇始已來，職官三世尚書已上，及品登王公而中間不降官緒，亦為姓。

translations.literal: If they were not originally great chiefs, but since Huangshi for three generations have held office as Minister of State Affairs and above, and whose rank reaches King or Duke without demotion of office in between, they too are surnamed lineages.
translations.idiomatic: If not of chiefly origin, yet since Huangshi three generations have held ministerial rank or higher, with continuous rank reaching king or duke and no break in promotion, they likewise count as surnames.

sentences.zh: 諸部落大人之後，而皇始已來官不及前列，而有三世為中散、監已上，外為太守、子都，品登子男者為族。

translations.literal: Descendants of tribal great chiefs who since Huangshi have not reached the above ranks, but for three generations have held office as Palace Attendant or above, or outside as prefect or commandant of a subprefecture, with rank reaching Marquis or Baron, are designated clans.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs of tribal chiefs who have not met the above standard, but for three generations held posts from Palace Attendant upward, or outside as prefect or subprefecture commandant, with rank to marquis or baron, are ranked as clans.

sentences.zh: 若本非大人，而皇始已來，三世有令已上，外為副將、子都、太守，品登侯已上者，亦為族。

translations.literal: If not originally great chiefs, but since Huangshi for three generations there have been prefectural magistrates and above, who outside serve as deputy general, subprefecture commandant, or prefect, with rank reaching Marquis and above, they too are clans.
translations.idiomatic: If not of chiefly descent, yet since Huangshi for three generations there have been county magistrates or above, with outside service as deputy general, subprefecture commandant, or prefect, and rank to marquis or higher, they also qualify as clans.

sentences.zh: 凡此姓族之支親，與其身有緦麻服已內，微有一二世官者，雖不全充美例，亦入姓族；

translations.literal: All collateral kinsmen of these surnamed lineages who share with them mourning within the garment of sackcloth, and who have even one or two generations holding office, though not fully meeting the ideal standard, shall also enter the surnamed lineage;
translations.idiomatic: Collateral kin within the closest mourning circle who can show an officeholder or two among the last generations, even if they fall short of the ideal rule, may still be admitted to a surname lineage;

sentences.zh: 五世已外，則各自計之，不蒙宗人之蔭也。

translations.literal: beyond five generations they shall each be counted separately and shall not enjoy the privilege conferred by clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: After five generations, each line is judged on its own and may not ride on a kinsman's standing.

sentences.zh: 雖緦麻而三世官不至姓班，有族官則入族官，無族官則不入姓族之例也。

translations.literal: Even with garment-of-sackcloth mourning, if for three generations office does not reach the surname rank, then if there is clan-level office they enter at the clan level; if there is no clan-level office they do not enter the surnamed lineage—such is the rule.
translations.idiomatic: Even for closest kin, if three generations fail to reach surname standing: with clan-level office they enter at clan rank; without it they do not enter a surname lineage—that is the rule.

sentences.zh: 凡此定姓族者，皆具列由來，直擬姓族以呈聞，朕當決姓族之首末。

translations.literal: All those fixing surname and clan lineages shall fully set forth their origins, directly propose the surname lineage and submit it for report; We shall decide the beginning and end of each surname lineage.
translations.idiomatic: All who seek surname or clan status must set out their origins in full and submit their proposed rank; the throne will decide each line's standing from top to bottom.

sentences.zh: 其此諸狀，皆須問宗族，列疑明同，然後勾其舊籍，審其官宦，有實則奏，不得輕信其言，虛長僥偽。

translations.literal: These various petitions must all be investigated among the clan, doubts clarified and agreements recorded, and only then their old registers traced and official careers verified; where there is substance, submit; do not lightly trust their words and foster false claims.
translations.idiomatic: Every petition must be checked against the clan, doubts resolved and agreements recorded, old registers verified against actual careers; only proven cases are forwarded—do not credulously accept claims that breed fraud.

sentences.zh: 不實者，訴人皆加『傳旨問而詐不以實之』坐，選官依『職事答問不以實』之條。

translations.literal: Those found untrue: all petitioners shall be charged under "Receiving an imperial order to inquire and deceitfully failing to answer truthfully"; selection officials shall be judged under the statute "In official duties, answering inquiries untruthfully."
translations.idiomatic: False claims: petitioners face the charge of deceiving an imperial inquiry; selecting officials face the penalty for untruthful answers in official business.

sentences.zh: 令司空公穆亮、領軍將軍元儼、中護軍廣陽王嘉、尚書陸琇等詳定北人姓，務令平均。

translations.literal: Order Duke of Works Mu Liang, General-in-chief of the Guards Yuan Yan, Defender-in-chief Prince Guangyang Jia, Minister of State Affairs Lu Yu, and others to examine and fix the surnames of northerners, striving to make them equitable.
translations.idiomatic: Charge Duke of Works Mu Liang, General of the Guards Yuan Yan, Defender-in-chief Prince Guangyang Jia, and Minister Lu Yu with adjudicating northern surnames on an equitable basis.

sentences.zh: 隨所了者，三月一列簿帳，送門下以聞。」

translations.literal: As each case is completed, once every three months compile the registers and send them to the Chancellery for report.
translations.idiomatic: For every case settled, submit quarterly registers to the Chancellery for imperial review.

sentences.zh: 於是昇降區別矣。

translations.literal: Closing the edict: Thereupon distinctions of elevation and demotion were established.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the hierarchy of advancement and demotion was set.

sentences.zh: 世宗世，代人猶以姓族辭訟，又使尚書于忠、尚書元匡、侍中穆紹、尚書元長等量定之。

translations.literal: In the age of Shizong, conqueror clansmen still litigated over surname lineages; the throne again appointed Ministers of State Affairs Yu Zhong and Yuan Kuang, Palace Attendant Mu Shao, Minister of State Affairs Yuan Chang, and others to measure and fix them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu, northern clansmen still sued over surname rank; Yu Zhong, Yuan Kuang, Mu Shao, Yuan Chang, and others were again ordered to adjudicate.

translations.literal: The book also writes tu (hare); Shen did not cite this.
translations.idiomatic: The text also reads tu (hare), which Shen did not mention.
